summary: Nicolaas Johannes Krom was an indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He earned his classics Ph.D. at Leiden University in 1908, studying under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Jacob Samuel Speyer. He worked for the Netherlands East Indies Archaeological Service (1913–1916) and was a professor at Leiden (1919; 1925–1945).

Linguist Nicolaas van Wijk studied at the University of Amsterdam under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien, and Moscow State University under Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov. He worked at the National Library of the Netherlands (1907) and became Professor of Slavic and Baltic linguistics at Leiden in 1913.
Working in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Nicolas Morrissey studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004) and held a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University, under doctoral supervisors Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling, MA supervisor Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h, and teachers Peter Masefield, Kannika Wimonkasem, and U-tain Wongsathit. He held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016–2017).
Nicolas Sihlé is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010).

Linguist and Tibetologist Nicolas Tournadre earned his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège. His career includes posts at INALCO, Paris 8 University, the University of Provence, Aix-Marseille University, the CNRS, and the University of Virginia.
Nicole Baden is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Richard Baker and succeeded him in 2024.

Indologist and linguist Nicole Balbir studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. She held academic posts at Patna University from 1952 to 1955 and at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from 1974 to 1992.

Scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology Nicole Vandier-Nicolas taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre (1951–1969) and served as a professor of Chinese civilization at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1969–1977).

Nicolás Altuchow was an indologist and linguist who studied under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak (~1934–1939). He later taught linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of the Republic from 1951 to 1982 and held a post at the National Museum of Natural History.
Nidheesh Kannan B. is an indologist who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (2016–2018). In 2021, he became an Assistant Professor at the same institution.

Indologist and linguist Niels Ludvig Westergaard studied at the universities of Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, and Oxford. He served as Lektor, Professor of Indian-Oriental Philology, and Rector (1867–1868) at the University of Copenhagen.

Niels Studsgaard Fuglsang was an indologist who studied at the University of Copenhagen (1778). He served as a minister at Zion Church in Tranquebar (1792–1804) and became a member of The Asiatic Society in 1801.
Working in history and archaeology, Nigel Allan succeeded Marianne Winder and served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (attested 1993).

Niharranjan Ray studied at Ananda Mohan College, Murari Chand College, University of Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden University under Jean Philippe Vogel. He served as Chief Librarian and Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts at Calcutta, and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Nijun Zhang is a student of religious studies and Tibetology. Zhang studied at Beijing Foreign Studies University, earned an MA from the University of Pittsburgh (2023–2025), and became a PhD student at the University of Virginia in 2025.

Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (attested 2010) under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes, having also studied under Géza Bethlenfalvy.

Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin was a scholar of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique from around 1826 to 1853.

Niklas Luhmann was a philosopher and sociologist who studied at the University of Freiburg, Bielefeld University, and Harvard University. He held an academic post at Bielefeld University from around 1968 to 1993.

Niklas Müller was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from around 1785 to 1788. In 1805, he served as Conservator at the Städtische Kunstsammlungen Mainz.
